messages.subject: New 'lavaanExtra' package
parts:
Just wrote this alternative lavaan syntax and simply looking for early feedback (proof of concept only). It can e.g., name mediation paths and write indirect effects automatically. Any reason why this might not be such a good idea? What edge cases wouldn't work? Would it be useful to anyone? And does a version of this exist already? Thanks,

Link: https://lavaanExtra.remi-theriault.com

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: Re: New 'lavaanExtra' package
parts:
Hi Rémi,

I like the approach. Thanks for putting so much work into it! About the indirect effects: That's great and will probably reduce specification errors. I posted a while ago an extension of x.boot that (hopefully) automatically identifies and calculates all indirect effects: https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/0RSsh4M6zQg/m/V2zKKV7FAwAJ A bit like Amos, but not limited to x->m->y. The extension is computationally intensive and not efficient. i haven't had the time or inclination to program a better solution yet. But maybe the two approaches can be combined? I don't know what that would look like exactly. It's just an idea.

Best

Christian

messages.subject: Re: New 'lavaanExtra' package
parts:
Thank you Christian for the feedback! I really appreciate it, and I have opened an issue to look at your suggestion of possibly integrating your x.boot extension to lavaanExtra: https://github.com/rempsyc/lavaanExtra/issues/1

In the meanwhile, I explored the main site (https://lavaan.ugent.be) to see where things might break and made a comparison tutorial where I go through each example comparing both methods: https://lavaanextra.remi-theriault.com/articles/example.html

Surprisingly, it supports almost all models, except multilevel SEMs (so far), since you need to specify level: 1, etc., so it changes the overall structure and logic. I will try to think of a solution. I was also afraid it wouldn't work with special functions and formatting like in example 4.2 but see the reprex below:
``` r
library(lavaanExtra)  
latent <- list(visual = c("x1", "start(0.8)*x2", "start(1.2)*x3"),
               textual = c("x4", "start(0.5)*x5", "start(1.0)*x6"),
               speed = c("x7", "start(0.7)*x8", "start(1.8)*x9"))
model <- write_lavaan(latent = latent)
cat(model)
#> ##################################################
#> # [---------------Latent variables---------------]
#>
#> visual =~ x1 + start(0.8)*x2 + start(1.2)*x3
#> textual =~ x4 + start(0.5)*x5 + start(1.0)*x6
#> speed =~ x7 + start(0.7)*x8 + start(1.8)*x9
```
<sup>Created on 2022-08-25 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

All the best,

messages.author: 2e1f893ffaa5b340
messages.subject: Re: New 'lavaanExtra' package
parts:
Hi Rémi
Thank you for posting this. An ideal use case would be automatically calculating total effects from early to later occasions in cross-lagged panel models. In econometrics these are called impulse responses, but with many occasions of measurement over time T, the 'by hand' calculations of all indirect effects becomes very unwieldy. Mplus makes this easy with the IND command, but lavaan does not. This would be an ideal use case for automated total effect calculations in lavaan as the sum of all indirect effects from early to later occasions across all AR and CL paths in cross-lagged panel models.

In case it's helpful, you can read about impulse responses in cross-lagged panel models in the following:

Zyphur, M. J., Allison, P. D., Tay, L., Voelkle, M. C., Preacher, K. J., Zhang, Z., ... & Diener, E. (2020). From data to causes I: Building a general cross-lagged panel model (GCLM). Organizational Research Methods, 23(4), 651-687.

Shamsollahi, A., Zyphur, M. J., & Ozkok, O. (2022). Long-run effects in dynamic systems: New tools for cross-lagged panel models. Organizational Research Methods, 25(3), 435-458.

Best wishes
Mike
